facts.text: Volga German immigrants founded Catharine in April 1876, naming the town after their former home of Katharinenstadt in Russia.
Catharine was named in honor of Catherine the Great, the Russian empress who invited Germans to settle along the Volga River.
Because Katharinenstadt was a major economic center in Russia, Catharine's early settlers were wealthier than other nearby Volga German groups.
Catharine began as a self-contained village with communal farming before transitioning to individual land ownership by the early twentieth century.
The community's first school opened in 1879 and served as a church until St. Catherine's Catholic Church was completed in 1892.
Catharine lies on the eastern side of North Fork Big Creek within the Smoky Hills region of the Great Plains.
